The SQL and Databases internship in short

The SkillMe SQL and Databases internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build one of 3 projects, such as ShelfWise: Library Management Database, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

ShelfWise: Library Management Database

Design and query a database that tracks books, members and loans for a college library.

  1. W1Tables, Data and Your First Queries
  2. W2Relationships, JOINs and Grouping
  3. W3Subqueries, Views and Indexes
  4. W4Library Insights Report

ShopLens: E-commerce Sales Analytics

Build a small online-store database and use SQL to find out what sells, who buys and when.

  1. W1Store Schema and Basic Queries
  2. W2Order Items, JOINs and Revenue by Category
  3. W3Customer Insights with CTEs, Views and Indexes
  4. W4Sales Analytics Report and Dashboard

StatsPitch: Cricket Stats Database

Load real cricket match data into a database and use SQL to uncover player and team stats.

  1. W1Teams, Players and Simple Stats
  2. W2Loading Real Data with JOINs and GROUP BY
  3. W3Advanced Stats with CTEs, Views and Indexes
  4. W4Cricket Analytics Report
Week by week

What each week of the SQL and Databases internship covers

Shown for ShelfWise: Library Management Database. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Tables, Data and Your First Queries

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Create a small library database with books, members and loans tables, fill it with sample data and answer simple questions with SELECT. This is the foundation every later week builds on, so getting clean tables now saves time later.

    What you learn

    • What tables, rows, columns and data types are
    • Writing CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements
    • Filtering and sorting with SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
    • Primary keys and why every row needs a unique id

    What you submit

    • schema.sql with three tables
    • seed.sql with sample data
    • queries_week1.sql with 8 commented queries
    • README with a screenshot of the tables in DB Browser
  2. Week 2 of 4

    Relationships, JOINs and Grouping

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Connect your tables with foreign keys and use JOINs and GROUP BY to answer questions that span several tables. You will also tidy the design so data is not repeated.

    What you learn

    • Foreign keys and constraints such as NOT NULL, UNIQUE and CHECK
    • INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN
    • Aggregates with GROUP BY and HAVING
    • Basic normalisation: removing repeated data into its own table

    What you submit

    • Updated schema.sql with foreign keys and constraints
    • queries_week2.sql with at least 9 JOIN and GROUP BY queries
    • Screenshot showing a constraint rejecting bad data
    • README section on normalisation
  3. Week 3 of 4

    Subqueries, Views and Indexes

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Answer harder questions with subqueries and CTEs, save useful queries as views, and make lookups faster with indexes. You will also learn to read a simple query plan.

    What you learn

    • Subqueries and Common Table Expressions (WITH)
    • Creating and using views
    • What an index is and when it helps
    • Reading EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN output at a basic level

    What you submit

    • queries_week3.sql with subqueries and at least one CTE
    • views.sql with two views
    • indexes.sql with at least one index
    • README section with before/after query plan screenshots
  4. Week 4 of 4

    Library Insights Report

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Turn your database into a short analytics report that answers 8-10 real questions a librarian would ask. Finish with an ER diagram, a clean README and a demo.

    What you learn

    • Framing business questions and answering them with SQL
    • Drawing an ER diagram
    • Presenting query results clearly
    • Optionally connecting SQL to a simple front-end

    What you submit

    • report.sql answering 8-10 questions
    • REPORT.md with results and insights
    • ER diagram image
    • Demo video or screenshots, plus an optional Streamlit app

SQL and Databases internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the SQL and Databases internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: ShelfWise: Library Management Database, ShopLens: E-commerce Sales Analytics or StatsPitch: Cricket Stats Database. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the SQL and Databases internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the SQL and Databases internship?

You need the basics of SQL, PostgreSQL, Data Modeling, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
